title: Mountain
notes: Strong case-study chapter: Scripture itself defines mountain as kingdom, then the same sense is pressed through Daniel, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Revelation, and the Gospel sayings with useful prevalence tables. The stone/rock/covenant chain is dense and on-voice. Main defects are local: two author sentences open with And; several presenter openers (See, Consider, Now consider, Now we have); one confused claim that the “final kingdom of the statue” is consumed after the prior sentence already named God’s kingdom as the final kingdom; and one overloaded multi-dash sentence on the fig-tree context. Surgical fixes restore house style without touching doctrine or quoted text.

This close of the mountain chapter is strong: two clean scripture cases, a dense related-symbol inventory, and a sharp method-versus-AI contrast that fits the book’s law-positive voice. Residual presenter staging still appears in a few lead-ins (“Now that you know… we should ask ourselves,” “Here we see,” “By now you should see the pattern”). One missing article and light hedging on the Babylon identification are the only other defects. Quotes and doctrine are clean; surgical cuts restore density without rewriting claims.

proposals.old: The final kingdom of the statue is consumed when God’s kingdom comes as a stone that grows into a mountain over the entire earth.
proposals.new: The kingdoms of the statue are consumed when God’s kingdom comes as a stone that grows into a mountain over the entire earth.
proposals.summary: Fix confused “final kingdom of the statue” wording.
proposals.rationale: The prior sentence already names God’s kingdom as the final kingdom; Daniel’s stone consumes the statue’s successive kingdoms, not a single “final kingdom of the statue.”

proposals.old: And thus symbols can be composed of both words and catch-phrases.
proposals.new: Symbols can thus be composed of both words and catch-phrases.
proposals.summary: Remove prohibited And-opening in author prose.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author sentences that start with And; the claim is unchanged.

proposals.old: And those who are humble, obedient even to death, will be exalted and lifted up.
proposals.new: Those who are humble, obedient even to death, will be exalted and lifted up.
proposals.summary: Remove prohibited And-opening in author prose.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author sentences that start with And; the exaltation claim stands as a direct assertion.

proposals.old: Now consider this poetic picture from Joel:
proposals.new: Joel paints the same picture in poetic form:
proposals.rationale: House style bans presenter staging such as Now consider; the rewrite keeps the transition and asserts the parallel.

proposals.old: See the same symbolic meaning applied in Jeremiah, describing Babylon the Great, which rules over the whole earth and destroys nation after nation.
proposals.new: The same symbolic meaning appears in Jeremiah, describing Babylon the Great, which rules over the whole earth and destroys nation after nation.
proposals.summary: Replace presenter “See the…” with a direct claim.
proposals.rationale: “See the same…” is a director cue; a plain assertion matches the house voice without changing the Jeremiah link.

proposals.old: Now we have Daniel, Revelation, Isaiah, and Jeremiah all agreeing on the meaning of this symbol of a Mountain as a Kingdom.
proposals.new: Daniel, Revelation, Isaiah, and Jeremiah all agree on the meaning of this symbol: mountain as kingdom.
proposals.summary: Drop “Now we have” staging and normalize capitalization.
proposals.rationale: Removes presenter framing and inconsistent title-case on mountain/kingdom while keeping the same four-witness claim.

proposals.old: Consider the account in Revelation of a flaming mountain thrown into the sea:
proposals.new: Revelation applies the same meaning to a flaming mountain thrown into the sea:
proposals.rationale: House style flags Consider as presenter staging; the rewrite states the application directly before the quote.

proposals.old: Because the context is a fig tree and a mustard tree — and sym:sym-tree[trees] are another symbol that Scripture defines as kingdoms or nations — and of course __“thrown into the sea”__ is a symbol clearly referring to Babylon the Great, as the link:/books/symbolic-language/the-fall-of-babylon/[Fall of Babylon] chapter demonstrated — and as the next chapter will trace from the Song of the Sea onward.
proposals.new: Because the context is a fig tree and a mustard tree — and sym:sym-tree[trees] are another symbol that Scripture defines as kingdoms or nations. The phrase __“thrown into the sea”__ is a symbol clearly referring to Babylon the Great, as the link:/books/symbolic-language/the-fall-of-babylon/[Fall of Babylon] chapter demonstrated — and as the next chapter will trace from the Song of the Sea onward.
proposals.summary: Split overloaded multi-dash sentence into two clear claims.
proposals.rationale: The original stacks three em-dash clauses and softens with “of course”; splitting preserves every claim and eases reading at the evidence seam.

proposals.old: Now that you know that mountain means a kingdom, we should ask ourselves: what does an sym:sym-island[island] represent?
proposals.new: Mountain means a kingdom. What does an sym:sym-island[island] represent?
proposals.summary: Strip soft staging and meta “ask ourselves.”
proposals.rationale: House style forbids presenter cues and meta-talk. Assert the established meaning and pose the next symbol directly.

proposals.old: It is the personification of island that led me to research the sym:sym-island[island] symbol, which we will cover in a future chapter.
proposals.new: It is the personification of the island that led me to research the sym:sym-island[island] symbol, which we will cover in a future chapter.
proposals.summary: Supply the missing article before island.
proposals.rationale: “Personification of island” is ungrammatical; “the island” matches the symbol under discussion.

proposals.old: Here we see an exceedingly high mountain from which all the other kingdoms of the earth can be seen.
proposals.new: This is an exceedingly high mountain from which all the other kingdoms of the earth can be seen.
proposals.rationale: Director-style phrasing is banned; “This is” keeps the claim direct and in the author’s voice.

proposals.old: In other words, he is taken to a kingdom ruling over all the other kings of the earth — likely Babylon the Great.
proposals.new: In other words, he is taken to a kingdom ruling over all the other kings of the earth — Babylon the Great.
proposals.rationale: House style requires asserting the case; the identification is already presented as the plain reading of the mountain.

proposals.old: By now you should see the pattern: Scripture reliably and consistently uses the word mountain as a way to say __“nation”__ or __“kingdom”__ in many different contexts across the whole of Scripture.
proposals.new: Scripture reliably and consistently uses the word mountain as a way to say __“nation”__ or __“kingdom”__ in many different contexts across the whole of Scripture.
proposals.summary: Cut “By now you should see the pattern” staging.
proposals.rationale: The director address violates house style; the remaining clause already asserts the pattern with full force.
